0.1.0.lead: This is where it starts. I called it 0.9.0 for a while, then admitted it was a first pre-release and renumbered it. You can already build lifts, pistes and paths on a mountain, guests ski it and rate it, and the whole thing works offline. It is rough, and I am showing it anyway.

0.2.0.lead: The second pre-release added a lot at once: goals and a ranger who gives advice, a ride-along view where you follow a guest down the hill, photo and walk modes, resort levels, six scenarios and a yearly report. Phones and tablets got touch controls, and there is a colour-blind-safe palette. It was a big pile of changes, so the highlights are the place to start.

0.2.1.lead: A small release about sound and about lift towers. The music was rewritten as nine tracks that follow the season and the time of day, the ambience got quieter, and tall lift towers were capped so the lines look less like pylons.

0.2.2.tagline: a real calendar and named runs
0.2.2.lead: This one changed how the game thinks about time. The year now has real months, with winter from December to March, and pistes are split into named runs you can open, groom and rename one by one. Energy, yearly lift service and a snowmaking switch came along with it.

0.2.3.lead: Guests now need a toilet, which I did not expect to be so entertaining. Level crossings, footbridges and bridges make the valley work, and four new marketing campaigns give you more to try. A few frameworks went in quietly for later content.

0.2.5.lead: There is no 0.2.4: I skipped it. This release is about being kinder in the first year, with more start money and cheaper quiet months. Bridges are now built while you draw the path, and a small card tells you when a new version is ready.

0.2.6.lead: You can dig a river now, from a spring to a lake, with calm stretches and white-water rapids. Gondolas, cable cars and detachable chairs can get mid-stations, and there is a new six-seat chair. It is the second batch of content for the summer-and-winter plan.

0.2.7.lead: Summer is half the reason I started this game, so this release is the one I was waiting for. A campground with a campfire, a petting zoo, a viewpoint, a treehouse, quad tours, a climbing crag, rafting and fishing all arrived together, with mountain bikers and anglers to use them.

0.2.8.lead: Two hotels, one with a heated pool that steams in the cold, and a little coffee stand where skiers pull over for a break. Seniors and school classes visit now, on their own calendar. The pool heating shows up in your energy bill, which I like.

0.2.9.lead: Winter got its own extras: a sleigh stable, a snowshoe hut and a snowscooter base. You can also paint backcountry routes, and the avalanche danger (1 to 5) decides whether they stay open. Snowboarders and ski tourers now show up as guests.

0.3.0.lead: Concerts on the mountain: a Mountain Concert in early September and a Snow Concert in March, each with a stage, speakers and soft lights over the crowd. This release also closed the big content phase that started with rivers, so the highlights include a one-line summary of all of it.

0.3.1.lead: No new big feature this time. I went through every building, lift and guest type with one test, fixed the ones that never earned money, and made the rules read the same everywhere. It is the kind of release that is boring to write about and nicer to play.

0.3.2.lead: This one is about how the valley looks. Some mornings now start with fog in the valley, a few sunrises and sunsets turn the sky and the snow pink, and the night sky has stars and a moon that changes shape. Nothing in the economy moved. If it is too much, or too little, there is an Atmosphere setting under Graphics.

0.3.3.lead: On a phone the game used to be mostly menus with a bit of map behind them. This release makes the map the main thing: drawers and inspectors are small sheets you pull up when you need them, the top bar and the HUD are one row each, and the cards step aside while you place something. I could only try it on an emulated phone, so I do not know yet how it feels under a real thumb. Desktop is unchanged.

0.4.0.lead: This release adds things to do besides skiing. You can paint a sled run and rent out sleds in winter, or build an alpine coaster in summer. The village gets a pizzeria, a bakery and a tourist office, and a grass strip lets people skydive, hang glide or paraglide on clear days. The winter carnival now has a parade. I have only played these in short test runs, so the balance may be off.

0.5.0.lead: This release is about how things look. Animals, buildings, lifts and vehicles have rounder shapes, the lift icons in the drawer are different for each kind of lift, the edge of the map is a layered cliff, and rivers and ponds have soft shorelines. On the High graphics setting there are now real shadows from the sun. I can only check this on a software renderer, so I do not know yet how it runs on a real graphics card or how it feels while you pan. Nothing in the economy changed.

0.5.1.lead: Bubble chairs and gondolas are smoother now, and a few more buildings lost their sharp corners. Sound now follows the camera: zoom in on an open bar to hear some music, or on a stream to hear the water, and the birds are quieter until you get close. There is also a Support page with a Ko-fi link. I could not listen to the new sounds myself, only measure them, so the levels may need adjusting. Nothing in the economy changed.

0.6.0.lead: This release adds the Schirmbar, a small domed bar you can put right beside a piste or a lift station. Skiers stop for a drink on the way down, and it plays some apres-ski music when you zoom in. It only opens in winter and in good weather, and you can close it yourself. Your resort also has a name now: pick one when you start a game or change it in Settings. The game has new music as well, a set of songs that follow the season, the time of day and the weather, and many of the sounds are now real recordings: footsteps, birds, bells, wind and thunder. Lakes and rivers have softer banks, buildings look rounder, and the sun shadows reach more of the scene. I have only tried all this on a software renderer and measured the sound rather than listened to every part of it, so the look and the levels still need a real playthrough.

0.6.1.lead: A small update this time. There are a couple of surprises up on the mountain now, rare ones, in winter, and I am not going to spoil them. There are two new achievements to find as well, and they stay hidden until you earn them. The surprises got more life as well: they are easier to notice, and they bring a small crowd boost for a month. Nothing in the economy changed. As before, I have only tried it on a software renderer, so how it looks and sounds in a real playthrough is still open.

0.6.2.lead: A small update about how things look and sound. The planes, paraglider canopies and hang gliders got new rounder shapes, and the jump plane now takes off clear of the buildings next to the strip. The groomers drive around buildings instead of through them and you can hear them at work, and snow keeps its size on big screens. I also made a 30 second trailer and a 90 second film, and you can watch both on the home page. Nothing in the economy changed. I have only tried it on a software renderer, so how it looks on a real screen is still open.

0.6.3.lead: A small update with one new kind of guest. Photographers turn up once you have a Viewpoint or a Treehouse. They like the golden hour and a beautiful sky, they walk to the best spot, take their pictures and have a hot drink. Good shots bring a little word of mouth, there is a new trophy called Golden hour, and Rudi has a tip about them. If you zoom in close you can hear the shutter. I have only tried it on a software renderer, so how it looks and sounds on a real screen is still open.

0.6.4.lead: A small update about autumn. Leaves now drift down from the deciduous trees and the larches near the camera, in gold, orange and red, and they thin out when the snow arrives or it rains. They follow the Atmosphere setting, and with reduced motion they just lie still. I also re-made the trailer and the 90 second film on the website so they show the leaves. You press play to start them, nothing loads before that. I have only seen it on a software renderer, so how it looks on a real screen is still open.

0.6.5.lead: A small update about how things look. In summer the Alpine Farms now send tractors out to mow the pasture, leave round bales and bring the hay home. The cows and the tractor got a proper going-over, because they looked a bit plain: cows have bells and coat patterns, and the tractor has a curved bonnet, mudguards and a slatted trailer. Lake and river banks are smoother and lakes reflect the sky. On High the hills and the trees just off screen cast shadows at dawn and dusk, and photographers raise their cameras and flash. I have only seen all of this on a software renderer, so how it looks on a real screen is still open.

0.6.6.tagline: cars, cows and a calmer farm
0.6.6.lead: Another small update about how things look and move. Cars and buses now come in several body styles with two-tone roofs, and in winter they carry snow on the roof that melts when they stand in the sun. They have soft shadows, brake lights that follow real slowing down and quiet headlight pools at night. Cows swish their tails and ring their bells, and sheep and goats twitch now and then. Tractors drive at a calmer pace and turn corners smoothly, and some trailers carry square bales. Where a river runs into a lake, the seam is gone. Again, I have only seen it on a software renderer.

0.7.0.tagline: a phone that shows the map
0.7.0.lead: This one is about playing on a phone. I tried the game on a real phone and it was too crowded: cards on top of cards, and the map squeezed into whatever was left. Now there is one slim row at the top and one card at a time. While you build, a small bar at the bottom shows what the tool is saying and has the buttons you need. The tab row shows a fade and an arrow when there is more to scroll, and the what's new card opens full screen instead of floating over things. Nothing changes on desktop. I have tested it on emulated phones, and I will keep checking it on a real one.

0.7.1.tagline: a chapel, and a tidier phone
0.7.1.lead: Two things this time. First, a small mountain chapel for the village: whitewashed, with a bell tower, a bench by the door and a few graves. It adds a little charm to the rating, and now and then, mostly on a summer Saturday, there is a wedding. The party walks up to the door, the bell rings, they stay for two hours and then have a meal at a lodge nearby. Second, some tidying that was on my list. While you place a lift or a piste on desktop, the ground profile is now a small line that opens into the full chart when you click it, the same as on a phone. Painting a hiking trail with your finger on a landscape phone works in my test again, and the month-end card on a phone no longer sits on top of the other cards. I have only seen the wedding on a software renderer, so I do not know yet how the little people look on a real screen.

0.7.2.tagline: the wedding party takes the path
0.7.2.lead: A small one. In 0.7.1 the wedding party walked in a straight line from the Base Lodge to the chapel, right across lawns and through fences. Now they follow your footpaths and roads, in a little line with the couple at the front, and then go on to the meal the same way. If there is no path they still cut across, as before. The guide also finally has a picture of the chapel.

0.8.0.lead: This one is for the steep runs. You can now mark a red or black run as a race course, build a Start Hut at the top and a Timing Hut at the foot, and gates go up along the run. Racers come to train on it, ski it a few times and pay a small fee. It will not make you rich, a black course roughly breaks even, but it looks good and the timing board is fun to watch.

0.8.1.lead: A follow-up for the race courses. You can now book a Club Race on a weekend, the run closes for a few hours, guests walk over to watch and the results go on the timing board. Each course gets a made-up sponsor, and the World Cup now runs on your own course. It is a small update, and old saves keep working.

0.8.2.lead: The race courses get a summer twin. A red or black mountain-bike trail with a Start Hut at the top and a Timing Hut at the foot can now be a downhill course, and downhillers come to ride it in laps. In summer you can book a Downhill Race on a weekend, the trail closes for a few hours and the winner's time goes on the board. Two small fixes came along: a course needs 50 m of drop instead of 60, and a run you repaint from blue to red is now called Red Run instead of staying Blue Run 1. Old saves keep working.
